title: Trial to Production Advocacy Playbook and Technical Proofbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is a combined sales-and-technical reference to convert short pilots and trials into production deployments. It focuses on framing value for engineering and procurement stakeholders, mitigating security and integration objections, and providing a repeatable trial -> production cadence for Redwood Inference.

Audience: Account Executives (AEs), Sales Engineers (SEs), Solutions Engineers, Customer Success (CS), and Platform/Infra engineers at prospects.

Use: Copy the timeline, checklist, battlecards, sample slides, pricing scenarios and security answers directly into call prep and pilot runbooks.

Executive one‑pager (ready-to-read)

- Headline: Run high-throughput, low-latency inference with predictable economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Three core customer outcomes: 1) Reduce per-token infrastructure cost, 2) Meet latency SLOs for user-facing features, 3) Simplify rollouts and governance across environments.
- Quick differentiator bullets: unified API across deployment modes, built-in caching/batching heuristics, SLA-backed dedicated pools, and private deployment options with KMS/HSM integration.

Positioning and messaging guidance

- Engineering-focused value thread: Start with concrete resource wins (latency p50/p95, token cost reduction), then show how Redwood integrates into CI/CD and observability.
- Platform/team lead message: Emphasize consistent API, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) and cost governance (per-route token accounting).
- Procurement/CISO hook: Outline compliance evidence (SOC2), private deployment packaging, and contract-level SLAs and indemnities.

Competitive brief (concise, for SEs and AEs)

- Typical competitors: Managed LLM APIs, cloud-native model endpoints, and self-hosted inference runtimes.
- Redwood advantages: 1) Predictable unit economics via batching/caching suggestions, 2) Multi-modal deployment (hosted -> dedicated -> private) without code changes, 3) Observability by model/route and token-level cost breakdowns.
- Typical objections and counters:
  - "We can host cheaper ourselves." -> Show TCO sample: include infra ops, reliability, and dev time; reference prototype numbers in pricing scenarios.
  - "We need strict data residency." -> Explain Redwood Private with VPC deployment and customer‑managed networking; provide timeline for on-prem package.
  - "Vendor lock-in concerns." -> Describe ability to pin model versions, export telemetry, and run private deployment with same control plane.

Suggested pitch deck outline (10–12 slides)

1. Title & logo (1 slide)
2. The problem: inference economics + reliability pain (1 slide)
3. Our thesis and Redwood product pillars (1 slide)
4. Technical architecture (hosted / dedicated / private) — one slide showing routing and fallback policies (1 slide)
5. Performance proof: p50/p95 latency and throughput for representative models (1 slide)
6. Cost model: batching, caching, quantization impacts (1 slide)
7. Security & compliance summary (1 slide)
8. Trial proposal & success criteria (SLOs, test prompts, runbook) (1 slide)
9. Case study snapshot with metrics (1 slide)
10. Commercial: pricing band and pilot terms (1 slide)
11. Next steps & asks (onboarding checklist) (1 slide)

Pricing guidance and sample scenarios

Notes: All pricing below is illustrative for conversation guidance. Use per-account pricing sheets for firm quotes.

Scenario A — Low‑latency customer-facing chat (hosted API pilot)
- Expected throughput: 10 rps, average response 150 tokens.
- Typical profile: high P95 sensitivity, medium token volume.
- Suggested pilot: hosted credits for 30 days, telemetry with p50/p95 and per-route token cost.
- Conversion anchor: blended unit cost target of $0.0020 per 1k tokens after optimizations (batching + caching).

Scenario B — High throughput embedding service (dedicated capacity pilot)
- Expected throughput: 200 qps embedding lookups, average 1024 tokens processed in occasional generation tasks.
- Pilot design: 2-week dedicated pool with autoscale policy and burst envelope.
- Conversion anchor: guaranteed throughput at <2ms per embed and committed monthly spend with tiered discounts.

Scenario C — Regulated workload (private deployment pilot)
- Expected constraints: VPC connectivity, KMS integration, strict retention rules.
- Pilot design: 30–60 day private deployment with staging and smoke tests.
- Commercial anchor: platform fee + support tier; typical timeline 8–12 weeks for on-prem or VPC + evidence packages.

Sample TCO talking points (for AEs)

- Include infrastructure ops cost (headcount FTE), time-to-recovery, and incremental engineering effort.
- Example: A mid-market product team running self-hosted inference estimated 0.6 FTE ops + 0.8 FTE infra engineering; convert to ~$180k/year in total labor vs. Redwood managed + dedicated options at negotiated committed spend.

Conversion success criteria (trial -> paid)

- Technical gates (must pass to convert):
  1) Achieve agreed latency SLOs (p95 target) on production-like load testing.
  2) Monitoring and alerting attached to customer Sentry/Datadog/Prometheus.
  3) Cost per 1k tokens within agreed band after two rounds of batching/caching tuning.
- Business gates: proof of concept integrated into one customer-facing flow with defined uplift metric (CTR, response time, automation throughput).
- Contract ask: 3–12 month committed tier depending on capacity type.

Trial runbook (30-day template)

Day 0: Kickoff
- SE + AE + customer platform lead onboarding call. Share trial scope, SLOs, success metrics, and access plan.
- Deliverables: test prompt set, baseline traces, network IPs for allowlisting.

Day 1–7: Baseline & integration
- Provide SDK quickstart snippet and route examples.
- Collect baseline telemetry (latency, token distribution).
- Run small-scale smoke tests and gather first failure modes.

Day 8–14: Optimization sprint
- Enable prefix/KV caching on eligible routes.
- Tune batching policy: set max latency budget and token batching thresholds.
- Validate quantized model variant if applicable.

Day 15–25: Scale test and resiliency
- Execute ramp to production-like QPS.
- Test routing policies and fallback to lower-cost model variants.
- Validate observability: trace sampling, per-route cost charts, alert thresholds.

Day 26–30: Business validation and close
- Run conversion workshop with procurement and security.
- Present runbook evidence and case study-style results.
- If gates met, present commercial terms and transition plan to CS/OPS.

Roles and ownership

- AE: commercial scope, procurement, legal intro.
- SE: technical lead for pilot, performance tuning, and demo.
- Solutions Engineer: integration support (onboarding scripts, infra).
- Customer Success: post-conversion onboarding and SLA management.

Customer-facing artifacts to deliver

- Pilot plan doc (this template adapted)
- Test prompt set and benchmark harness (repo links)
- Short slide pack (3–5 slides) summarizing performance & cost impact
- Security evidence pack (SOC2 summary, pen test report snippet, architecture diagrams)

Case study template (for internal reuse)

- Customer profile: size, industry, primary use case.
- Success metrics: latency improvements, cost per inference, availability, and business metric uplift.
- Timeline and deployment mode.
- Lessons learned and recommended follow-on phases.

Example case snapshot (fictionalized for prospect conversations)

- Customer: Brightline Retail (ecommerce personalization)
- Mode: Dedicated pool with canary rollout to 10% traffic
- Results after 60 days: p95 latency from 620ms -> 180ms, per-token cost reduced 46% after batching and prefix caching, A/B test conversion uplift +3.0% on personalized recommendations.

Security & compliance FAQ (engineer + CISO friendly)

Q: How do you isolate customer data in Hosted mode?
A: Logical multi-tenancy with strict tenant separation at the runtime and storage layers. Data-at-rest encrypted (AES-256). Customer data is tagged and retained per route retention rules; we provide audit logs on request.

Q: Do you support KMS/HSM for key management?
A: Yes. Redwood Private and Dedicated offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM options for on-prem packages.

Q: What compliance evidence can we provide?
A: SOC2 Type II report, internal penetration testing summary, data processing addendum (DPA), and regional data residency attestations. Red team results and remediation timelines available under NDA.

Q: What is the private deployment timeline?
A: Typical VPC-hosted private deployment: 4–8 weeks for medium complexity. On-prem packaging with customer air-gap requirements: 8–12 weeks depending on customer change control.

Q: How is PII handled for prompt/response logging?
A: Logging is configurable at route granularity. Customers can disable request/response logging, enable PII redaction rules, or route logs to customer-owned storage endpoints.

Q: What SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
A: We provide tiered SLAs based on committed spend; standard SLA for Dedicated 99.9% uptime with defined latency targets for provisioned pools. Exact terms outlined in the contract appendix.

Appendix: example onboarding snippets and run commands

- SDK quickstart (curl):
  curl -X POST \\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n    -d '{"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":128}'

- Sample alert thresholds (suggested):
  - p95 latency > target + 60ms: SEV-2
  - error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes: SEV-1

- Observability hooks: provide Datadog trace endpoint, Prometheus metrics exporter, and optional direct ingestion to customer S3 for token-level billing reconciliation.

Email templates (short)

- Kickoff invite: "SE/Kickoff: Trial start — access & scope" (include checklist and IPs)
- Conversion close: "Pilot results and commercial proposal — next steps" (attach short slide pack and runbook evidence)

Appendix B: common troubleshooting checklist

- Network: allowlist outbound IPs, confirm egress routes and TLS certs.
- Auth: validate API key or mTLS credentials, verify KMS roles if used.
- Performance: verify batching budget, check token distribution skew, validate KV cache hit rate.
